data: Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

Not every Apollo job needed the Moon rocket. The Saturn IB was the pragmatic option — a crew-rated lifter for the work that stayed in Earth orbit: Apollo 7's shakedown of the redesigned spacecraft, the ferry flights to Skylab, and the handshake-in-orbit of Apollo-Soyuz. Its first stage was famously a bundle of tanks borrowed from the earlier Redstone and Jupiter missiles, clustered together — proven parts doing a new job rather than a clean-sheet design. It's the least glamorous rocket in the program, and a quiet lesson in not overbuilding: match the machine to the mission.
Saturn IB is an orbital launcher built by Chrysler / Douglas / IBM in USA. Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP.
Fatal pre-launch pad fire 1967-01-27 killed Grissom + White + Chaffee
First crewed Apollo flight — Earth-orbit CSM shakedown
First crewed Skylab visit — repaired the damaged workshop and saved the programme
Second Skylab crew — 59 days, deployed twin-pole solar shield to replace parasol
Longest Skylab stay — 84 days, observed Comet Kohoutek, disputed "Skylab strike" rest day
First international human spaceflight cooperation; first US-USSR rendezvous + docking
Original Apollo CSM design — never flew crewed; killed Apollo 1 crew on the pad 1967-01-27. Redesign produced the Block II flown 1968-1975
NASA pad at Cape Canaveral (1961-68) — first Saturn I; Apollo 1 fire site 1967-01-27; Apollo 7 first crewed launch 1968-10-11
Apollo 10 + Skylab + 53 Shuttle flights; now NASA's SLS / Artemis pad
First Soyuz generation; Komarov's fatal flight
First US human-rated launcher — variant of the Army's Redstone IRBM. Launched Freedom 7 (1961-05-05) and Liberty Bell 7 (1961-07-21)
1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — Pioneer 10/11, Helios 1/2, Mariner 9/10, Pioneer Venus
The engine that sent Apollo to the Moon — twice
Eight engines, eight missions — the Saturn I workhorse
Saturn IB SA-209, the never-flown Skylab rescue and Apollo–Soyuz backup rocket
